title: Pluggable event-adapter + checkpointed async iterator for streaming chat ergonomics
creator: Ava Ghosh
description: Design and implement a developer-friendly pattern for handling streaming chat completions in the Python SDK that: 1) surfaces discrete semantic events (delta tokens, role changes, function calls, structured output), 2) supports pluggable adapters for transform/validation, and 3) provides checkpoint/resume semantics combined with idempotent retry guidance for transient transport failures.
background: Current Python SDK streaming tickets focus on iterators, decorators, and retry semantics but several customers have asked for an approachable pattern that: 1) makes event shape discovery easy, 2) allows users to attach small transforms (e.g., deserialize JSON blocks, map custom function call handlers), and 3) recovers from network disconnects without duplicating side-effectful events (function calls / webhook forwards). We need an SDK primitive that packages these concerns and is ergonomic for both sync and async flows.
proposed_solution:
Introduce a PluggableEventAdapter interface plus a CheckpointedStream async iterator primitive. Key ideas:
- EventAdapter: user-supplied object with methods (map_event, filter_event, coerce_event) that run synchronously in the SDK event loop. We provide built-in adapters: JSONBlockAssembler, RoleNormalizer, FunctionCallDetector, and DeduplicationHintEmitter.
- CheckpointedStream: async iterator that yields canonical SDK Event objects and exposes .checkpoint() + resume(token) APIs. Checkpoints capture minimal resume tokens (transport offset + last-emitted-event-id + adapter-state-hash).
- Retry guidance: SDK implements transparent idempotent retries only for "stateless" events (token deltas). For events flagged as side-effectful (function_call_start/complete) the adapter emits deduplication hints and the platform includes guidance to users to make server-side idempotency keys use the checkpoint metadata.
- Backpressure hooks: adapters can signal preferred batch_size or a yield_delay hint; CheckpointedStream respects these hints when buffering from the transport.
- Sync + Async parity: provide a streaming sync wrapper that runs the async iterator in a background thread and exposes a generator with the same Event shapes.
api_examples:
# Async usage example:
from redwood import StreamingClient, JSONBlockAssembler, CheckpointedStream

client = StreamingClient()
adapter = JSONBlockAssembler()
stream = CheckpointedStream(client.start_chat_stream(prompt="hi"), adapters=[adapter])

async for ev in stream:
    if ev.type == 'delta':
        print(ev.text)
    elif ev.type == 'function_call' and ev.phase == 'complete':
        # use checkpoint token to dedupe on retry
        checkpoint = await stream.checkpoint()
        handle_function_call(ev.payload, dedupe_hint=checkpoint)

# resume from checkpoint later:
new_stream = CheckpointedStream(client.resume_stream(checkpoint['resume_token']), adapters=[adapter])
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes EventAdapter interface and registers built-in adapters: JSONBlockAssembler, RoleNormalizer, FunctionCallDetector, DeduplicationHintEmitter
CheckpointedStream async iterator yields Event objects with stable schema and supports await stream.checkpoint() returning a small JSON-serializable token
Resume path using resume(token) replays correctly without duplicating idempotent deltas and provides dedupe hints for side-effectful events
Backpressure hints from adapters influence SDK buffering and are respected during high-throughput tests
Sync wrapper provides parity for common user flows and documented caveats
Unit tests cover adapter lifecycle, checkpoint round-trip, resume correctness, and a simulated network disconnect + retry scenario
Integration test against a local streaming test harness showing correct dedup behavior for function_call events when client uses checkpoint token as idempotency key
rollout_plan: Alpha: merge behind feature flag and release to internal dogfooders (week 1)
Beta: enable for signed-up external users with explicit opt-in and collect telemetry on resume usage (week 2-3)
GA: flip feature flag after observed stability and docs + examples published (week 4)
Post-GA: iterate on adapter catalog and add TypeScript parity work as follow-up
risks_mitigation: Risk: checkpoints leak PII or sensitive context -> Mitigation: checkpoint token contains only transport offset, last_event_id hash, and adapter-state-hash; document and provide opt-out
Risk: resume duplicates side-effectful events -> Mitigation: require adapters to mark events with 'side_effect' boolean; SDK surfaces dedupe_hint and docs show how to use server-side idempotency keys
Risk: adapter callback abuse can block streaming -> Mitigation: run adapter.map_event with execution time quotas and fall back to a 'slow-adapter' mode that logs and drops the adapter
Risk: increased SDK complexity -> Mitigation: provide simple defaults and a one-line "no-adapter" flow that gives classic token deltas
notes: We should align checkpoint token shape with the Java/TS SDK plans so platform resume semantics remain consistent.
Add telemetry for: checkpoint frequency, resume success/fail, adapter errors, average adapter latency.
Design doc draft: link to internal Confluence (confluence.redwood/sdks/streaming-adapters) - replace with final link in PR
Consider making DeduplicationHintEmitter part of default adapter chain to reduce user work
